key_insight: This study evaluates a pathology foundation model combined with multiple instance learning to grade Barrett’s esophagus dysplasia across institutions without stain normalization. It uses 969 whole-slide images from four institutions; the supplied abstract does not include performance results.
problem_solved: Pathologists often disagree on Barrett’s esophagus dysplasia grades, especially low-grade dysplasia, complicating clinical decisions. The study addresses automated grading across institutions with differing slide-staining characteristics.
method: Conduct a retrospective, multi-institutional diagnostic accuracy study using 969 H&E-stained whole-slide images.
Train patch-level classifiers on expert annotations to identify diagnostically relevant tissue regions.
Combine a pathology foundation model with multiple instance learning for dysplasia grading without stain normalization.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the study examines whether foundation-model features and multiple instance learning can support cross-institution pathology workflows without stain preprocessing. Quantitative accuracy and generalization cannot be assessed from the truncated abstract.

paper_title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
paper_authors: Amirali Khosravi, Jaidip M. Jagtap, D. Chamil Codipilly, Catherine E. Hagen, Jason T. Lewis
